baseline.definition: replicate-averaged (49 conditions x 7 channels) log-response cell means; rank-1 R2 = 1 - sum(s[1:]^2)/sum(s^2) after centring each channel (common.rank1_profile)

definitions.rank1_r2: SVD of the column-centred matrix M (cells x channels); R2_1 = 1 - sum_{k>=2} s_k^2 / sum_k s_k^2
definitions.amplification ratio: slope_a1[ch6] / slope_a1[ch0]; slope_a1[ch] = mean over the 7 a2 levels of the OLS slope of log cell-mean response on the a1 level index 0..6 (step1/t04 definition)
definitions.analysis unit: one complete (a1,a2) input-grid condition; adjacent cells and replicates are not independent

drop_top1pct_cv_cells.definition: remove every replicate of cells whose within-cell coefficient of variation (replicate sd/mean, pandas ddof=1, computed on response_value) is >= the 99th percentile

winsorise_p1_p99_within_channel.definition: clip response_value to the 1st/99th percentile computed within each of the 7 channels (linear interpolation), then log-transform and average replicates

drop_global_minmax_per_channel.definition: remove the single largest and single smallest response_value (row-level, raw scale) independently within each channel; 14 rows removed; cell means recomputed from the remaining 2 replicates for the affected cells

channel_block_partitions.definition: channel shape = bin-averaged-over-conditions log profile on the (a1,bin)x(a2) grid, mean-centred; CORR = 7x7 Pearson correlation across the 49 profile entries; statistic = mean within-block CORR - mean between-block CORR; permutation null = 20000 random shuffles of the 7 block labels (seed 2024)

bootstrap.definition: 4000 resamples of the 49 complete (a1,a2) grid conditions with replacement; each resample carries all 8 signal bins of the drawn condition; the 392x7 matrix is rebuilt and the rank-1 R2 and the two OLS channel slopes are recomputed

ratio_a1_ch6_over_ch0.note: the ch0 slope is ~0.017 and can be negative by chance, so the ratio distribution is heavy-tailed and its percentile CI is unstable; the peak/subgrid ratio and the slope-ordering concordance are the stable summaries

slope_ratio_rank_concordance.definition: for each resample, the ordering of the 7 a1 slopes; fraction of resamples in which the slope ordering is strictly increasing ch0<...<ch6 and in which ch6 is the maximum

complete_unit_leaveout.definition: rank-1 basis (leading right singular vector) and channel mean are estimated on the training channels/units only; the held-out channel is predicted from the training latent coordinate with an intercept refit on the held-out values; R2 is scored against the held-out channel's own variance (no between-channel intercept credit)

single_gain_axis_null.definition: 500 synthetic 49x7 surfaces; within each channel the 49 (a1,a2) values are independently permuted, exactly preserving that channel's mean and standard deviation but destroying any cross-channel correspondence; rank-1 R2 recomputed each time

contradictions_and_caveats: per-channel min-max and per-channel z-score normalisations destroy the rank-1 structure (R2 0.5588 and 0.5681): the gain-axis claim is a property of the log/linear magnitude scale, not scale-free.

the 29x amplification ratio rests on a noise-floor denominator: the peak/subgrid ratio (ch6/ch5, both on the shared rising trend) is only 1.25, and the bootstrap CI on the ratio is wide and can include zero denominators.

the channel-regime boundary at 0-2|3-6 is not uniquely identified: 2 of the 63 two-block partitions reach perm p<0.05 and the best-vs-second-best gap difference is 0.0795, below the permutation null sd (0.1610).
leave-one-channel out shows the rank-1 axis has no predictive content for channels 0-2 (R2 0.0190/0.0030/0.0226): the shared latent is carried by the high-gain channels 4-6.
